answer: Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 451 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is cheap once and expensive in bulk. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the voyage seed, the onyx timing is verifiable from the comet record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. A farm that wants 146 keys thus pays 146 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. That is 31 dollars per alias. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
